subject: Perf sprint plan & throughput targets — ACME Logistics
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Perf sprint plan & throughput targets — ACME Logistics

Hi Jamal,

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary workload: document ingestion + contextual retrieval for dispatch assistant; typical prompt context ~1.2k tokens.
- Peak 95th latency requirement: <= 350ms (p50 target 120–150ms) for single-turn generation.
- Concurrent active users: ~120 during peak; burst concurrency to 300 for 30s events.
- Streaming: yes — token-by-token streaming to UI is required for perceived latency.
- Cost sensitivity: target ~50% reduction vs current self-hosted spend (today's baseline provided by Priya).

Technical acceptance criteria (we propose to validate):
1) Sustained qps to cover 120 concurrent with p95 <=350ms on your priority model variant.
2) Streaming latency: first token <80ms at p50 under steady load.
3) Graceful degradation: fallback to cheaper model variant with preserved 95% of semantic quality (as judged by your eval prompts).

Proposed next steps:
- Tessa/Karthik/Marissa: run a 2-week perf qualification sprint with ACME (scope below).
- ACME: share a sanitized sample trace and typical prompt set (we need ~200 prompts to run regressed quality tests).
- Schedule an architecture sync: Wed 11/04 10:00 PT (or propose alternate).

Deliverables from Redwood for the sprint:
- Test harness + load profile validated against your traffic shape.
- Quantization/profile suggestions and expected cost delta (+ confidence bands).
- Concrete config for continuous batching, KV caching prefixes, and fallback routing.

Attaching initial requirements + a small KV cache diagram to illustrate where caching would sit in the stack.

Thanks — I’ll book the sync unless you prefer a different slot.

— Tessa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_perf_requirements.pdf (pdf), kv_cache_diagram.png (image)

From: Jamal Peters <jamal.peters@acme-logistics.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Perf sprint plan & throughput targets — ACME Logistics

Tessa — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) The 120 concurrent is active agents interacting with the UI; our internal queueing means backend concurrency can spike briefly to ~260 for 10–20s.
2) For streaming, first-byte is more important than sustained per-token latency — we want first token to appear quickly so UI can start rendering.
3) We can provide the sanitized prompt set; Priya will drop it in the shared folder and include a couple of failure cases we care about.

We’re comfortable with a two-week qualification sprint. Confirming Wed 11/04 10:00 PT works. Also, we have an internal SRE contact (optinfer@thirdparty.ai) who manages our existing quantized deployment — I’ll loop them in if you want vendor-level telemetry.

Jamal
Head of Product — ACME Logistics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Perf sprint plan — ACME (internal)

Thanks — quick technical notes / asks before Wed: 

1) Load profile: please confirm tail distribution — do they expect sustained 120 concurrent for >15 min, or multiple short spikes? I’ll craft a combined steady+burst profile (steady: 120 conc for 20m; burst: +200 conc for 30s every 10m).
2) Models: we should bench both the v2 (fp16) and v2-q4_0 quant variants. If v2-q4_0 meets their quality bar we can reduce per-token compute by ~40–55%.
3) Caching: propose prefix/KV caching anchored at retrieval layer. If average shared context ratio >18% we can get substantial p95 wins. Need sample traces to compute hit-rate assumptions.
4) Streaming: implement early-token flush path in the runtime (first-token prioritized scheduling). I’ll draft the patch and a perf test.
5) Fallbacks & routing: Canary to cheaper variant when queue depth > X and p95 starts rising; need to agree on X.

Deliverables for Wed: a short bench run (local), a suggested batch and cache config, and a high-level cost delta estimate. I’ll also prepare a small experiment plan to validate quality regression on their prompt set.

— Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Perf sprint plan — ACME (internal)

All — adding cost/ops perspective: 

- Continuous batching: target batch windows of 5–12ms for steady state to save ~20–30% on tokens; ensure we cap max batch to avoid p95 spikes.
- Quantization profiles: v2-q4_0 gives best cost wins if quality checks pass. Offer a staged rollout: 10% of traffic -> 50% -> 100% with rollback guards.
- Cache strategy: short TTLs (30s–2m) for per-user conversational prefixes; longer TTL (5–20m) for shared retrieval prefixes used across many users. This balances freshness vs hit rate.
- Monitoring: add an eval-led quality monitor using their 200 prompts and tie regressions to automatic rollback if semantic similarity drops >4 pts.

I’ll prepare a cost estimate workbook for Wed — baseline vs: (1) fp16 steady, (2) q4_0 mixed, (3) fallback routing active. Expect to send redwood_cost_estimate_v1.xlsx by EOD.

— Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Performance
